extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD managers, analysts, and students performing OMB Circular A-76 cost comparisons (e.g., Naval personnel evaluating in-house vs contract performance)
extracted.subtask_description: Performing a formal cost-comparison analysis (in-house versus contract-out) for a government information system (HRMIN) according to Office of Management and Budget Circular No. A-76. The work includes identification and accumulation of all cost elements, development of contract costs, benchmarking alternatives, and present-value economic analysis to reach recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review threshold for A-76 analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy requires a review of each commercial or industrial activity costing more than $100,000 by every agency of the government which runs one, to determine if existing performance, in-house or contract, continues to be in accordance with the policy and guidelines set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an activity exceeds the $100,000 threshold it must be reviewed under OMB Circular No. A-76; use that review to determine whether to retain in-house performance or convert to contracted performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary framework: in-house vs contract cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework of this review is a cost comparison of in-house performance costs and the costs of contracting-out the performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions of the study must be based on application of the requirements of OMB Circular A-76 to the results of this cost comparison; collect relevant cost data for both alternatives and compare on comparable bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting relevant information and cost data
rubrics_metrics.description: The research effort involved collecting information and relevant cost data about and from the HRMSS, HRMIN and computer service companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data sources should include internal system records, organizational profiles, and market/contractor proposals or timesharing charges; ensure completeness and comparability of datasets used for both in-house and contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Labor — include all direct labor costs as part of in-house performance cost element identification and accumulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out by pay grade/position, hours, and rates; use FY (fiscal year) data where appropriate and document assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits on labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe Benefits on Labor — account for fringe benefits applied to labor costs (e.g., retirement, health, payroll taxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute fringe as a percentage or per-employee addition to direct labor; use current organizational benefit rates and apply consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect labor (operations overhead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect Labor — include indirect labor as an operations overhead expense when accumulating in-house performance costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify support staff and supervisory time that cannot be charged directly to tasks, allocate appropriately across cost centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect materials and supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect Materials and Supplies — capture non-direct material and supply costs under operations overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include consumables, office supplies, and other materials supporting system operations but not billed as direct inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation — include depreciation of equipment and capital assets as part of operations overhead expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate depreciation schedules for computing annual costs; include costs for computer hardware, peripherals, and facilities equipment used by the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rent
rubrics_metrics.description: Rent — account for space rental costs (or imputed rent) as an element of operations overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If government-owned space is used, include an imputed rent or opportunity cost per guidance; document rate bases and allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and repair
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance and Repair — include costs for maintenance and repair of equipment and facilities supporting the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture service contracts, spare parts, preventative maintenance labor, and associated overhead; allocate to the system's cost profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support Costs — include other support costs identified in operations overhead (e.g., helpdesk, administrative support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and categorize support activities and ensure their costs are allocated to the evaluated system performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities — include utility costs (power, communications, etc.) that support system operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate electricity, telecom, and other utilities attributable to system operation; document basis for allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Insurance — include insurance costs related to assets and operations as part of overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture premiums or internal insurance charges where applicable; allocate proportionally to system costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Direct Costs — identify and include other direct costs not captured under labor or overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include travel, contractor-specific purchases, specialized supplies; list and quantify all such direct expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: General and Administrative Expenses (G&A)
rubrics_metrics.description: General and Administrative Expenses (G & A) — include corporate or organizational level administrative costs allocated to the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent G&A allocation bases and rates; document the calculation and justification for allocation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inflation — include inflation adjustments in cost computations over multi-year horizons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use defensible inflation assumptions for future-year cost projections; apply consistently to both in-house and contract alternatives prior to discounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of Capital — include cost of capital in the economic analysis where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate cost of capital or required rate of return when capital expenditures or financing considerations affect comparative economics.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time costs and other costs
rubrics_metrics.description: One-Time Costs and Other Costs — identify and include one-time implementation or transition costs in the comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include conversion, startup, termination, or implementation expenses that differ between alternatives (e.g., contractor transition costs, in-house development phases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting-out cost development
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting-Out, Contract Cost Development — prepare a detailed contract-out cost estimate for the performance to be contracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop typical contractor charges, benefits, disadvantages, and adjustments (e.g., timesharing rates); ensure contract assumptions align with scope and service levels of in-house performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarking — identify benchmark activities and metrics to compare in-house performance to market/contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparable commercial benchmarks where possible (e.g., typical charges from service bureaus); document differences in scope or quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative assessment and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative assessment — evaluate multiple alternatives (e.g., keep HRMIN at NPRDC, use computer service bureaus) including typical charges, benefits, and disadvantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay out alternatives, create assessment matrices, quantify pros/cons and perform comparative cost accounting to reach recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: User profile determination
rubrics_metrics.description: User Profile Determination — determine user profiles to estimate resource usage and allocate costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify number and type of users, usage patterns, and compute associated costs (e.g., timesharing usage, per-user charges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timesharing service cost adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Timesharing Service, Cost Adjustments — adjust timesharing service costs for comparability with in-house operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust contractor timesharing rates for differences in services provided, overhead treatment, or usage assumptions to achieve an 'apples-to-apples' comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted contract-out performance cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjusted HRMIN Contract-Out Performance Cost — compute contract-out costs after applying necessary adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present an adjusted contract cost schedule comparable to the in-house cost accumulation, including the same cost categories where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present value analysis / net present value
rubrics_metrics.description: Present Value Analysis — perform present value analysis (net present value) for in-house and contract performance cost streams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discount future costs to present value using an appropriate discount rate; include appendices or exhibits showing PV computations for both alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses of economic analysis in decision making
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses of Economic Analysis — utilize economic analysis to inform decisions about contracting versus in-house performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret cost comparisons, PV results, and qualitative factors to form results, conclusions, and recommendations in line with policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phases of system development (accounting for development costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phases of System Development — consider phases of system development when identifying costs (appendix: phases of development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include development-phase costs, amortize or treat as one-time investments as appropriate, and reflect in cost streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of OMB Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of OMB Circular A-76 — follow the implementation guidance (Appendix D) to execute the required review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the procedural steps and compliance requirements specified by OMB Circular A-76 when conducting the cost comparison and when documenting results and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and transparency (results, conclusions, recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Results, Conclusions and Recommendations — base conclusions on the cost comparison and the application of the circular's requirements, and document recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear presentation of data, computations, assumptions, and the reasoning that led to recommended actions (e.g., retain in-house or convert to contract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure compliance with federal, DOD and Navy policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the review and the HRM system objectives comply with federal law and Department of Defense and Navy policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing alternatives, verify that proposed actions conform to statutory and departmental policy requirements and the HRMSS mission/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensitivity and summary matrices (alternative location summary assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Location Summary Assessment Matrix and summary exhibits — use matrices and tables to summarize comparative assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide matrices that summarize criteria across alternatives (cost, benefits, risks) and include sensitivity checks to demonstrate robustness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for typical benefits and disadvantages of alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical Benefits and Typical Disadvantages — identify non-cost benefits and disadvantages (e.g., capabilities, control, risk) for each alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List qualitative factors (capabilities, security, responsiveness) and weigh them alongside quantitative cost results to reach a balanced decision.
